Definition: Does the government maintain a digital address register?

redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited, but independent research confirms the score. Madagascar has no systematic digital address register: it uses a 3-digit postal code system (Paositra Malagasy, 111 codes) and an informal, non-standardised parcel 'lot' numbering scheme (e.g. B153, IVC65) rather than street names/numbers, per OSM Madagascar tagging guidelines. No evidence of any national addressing database. Confirmed as 'No' (1); code unchanged.

Definition: Does the government maintain a separate cadastral register?
Comments: No credible evidence found for separate digital cadastral register; mentions of cadastre in mining but not general.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 'No' score is outdated and unsupported. Madagascar's Programme National Foncier II (2024-2030) is actively digitising cadastral data: Plans Locaux d'Occupation Foncière (PLOF) built from orthophotos, 17 software tools developed for partial dematerialisation, and an MDAT open day (2 Aug 2025) announced the creation of 'cadastres numériques' and a unified land information system (SIF), alongside automated land-certificate kiosks (DAI) launched July 2025 in Antananarivo. However, PNF II's own 2026 documentation states no single integrated SIF/cadastral database yet exists nationally ('Aucun logiciel intégré spécifique pour le SIF n'est encore disponible'). Revised to 'Under development' (3); confirmed by authoritative government/programme sources, not a single weak source.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No credible evidence found for digital population register. INSTAT conducts censuses but no ongoing digital register mentioned in official sites or reports.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 'No' score is now clearly outdated. Madagascar's World Bank-financed PRODIGY project is running a national biometric household-enrolment campaign ('Izaho Tokana') explicitly designed to 'form the basis of the country's unified social register', assigning a Unique Identification Number (UIN) to each person: 410,000 households/1.32m individuals enrolled by May 2024, rising to over 3.25 million adults enrolled by 10 June 2026 (World Bank feature, 1 July 2026) after 2.6 million enrolments in two months alone (Biometric Update, 5 June 2026). This is an actively operating, nationally-deployed register-building exercise, not merely planned, but coverage remains partial against the ~30 million population. Revised to 'Partially deployed' (4), based on corroborating World Bank project documentation and independent trade press.
